action_items.text: Come up with a components concept
Look into materials that are durable (harder plastic, symbols that won't fade)
Research whether a universal remote control is possible (including mode switching for different TV brands)
Research whether sending a signal to a TV to pop up a menu is technically possible
Present ideas on paper (shape, curves, colours) next time
draw some designs for the remote (e.g., layout, buttons, placement)
post designs periodically on the product share
draw ideas for buttons/layout (general design work)
find out if rechargeable batteries are possible/feasible for the remote
find out what people are willing to pay for comfort features (e.g., rechargeable, L_C_D_ screen)
research if L_C_D_ screen can be integrated (cost, space, feasibility)
research if speech recognition is possible/feasible (cost, space)
look into possibility of a docking station for rechargeable batteries
find out if it's possible to make the remote act as a charger (wireless/plug-in)
check if sending emails internally is allowed (regarding documents)
find out financial/cost information for rechargeable batteries, L_C_D_ screen, speech recognition
draw/work on basic design (channels, buttons placement)

decisions.text: Go for a universal remote control
Do not include an L_C_D_ screen (too expensive, power-hungry)
Do not implement speech recognition at this time (technology not mature, market not ready)
Hide less important settings (sound, display) under a menu
Target younger people (<40), focus on design appeal and willingness to pay
Use changeable covers/skins for the remote (instead of entire remote redesign), keep basic remote design simple
